newsitem.title: DUBAI: Clinton urges dialogue between Islam and West.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges dialogue between Islam and West.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton has said that radical elements in both Moslem and Western countries must not be allowed to stand in the way of continued dialogue between Islam and the West.
Clinton made his comments in a message to a cultural festival being held in Saudi Arabia this week. A copy was sent to Reuters on Tuesday by the U.S. embassy in Riyadh.

"We have a collective responsibility, you in Saudi Arabia and the Moslem world at large and we in the West. We must ensure that radical elements in our societies do not dictate the debate and exploit misunderstandings. A constructive dialogue must continue," Clinton said.
"...We cannot hope to remove or even lower barriers that may still exist without talking and listening to each other, without trying to understand and tolerate and seek common grounds," he added.

Radical Moslems, opposed to the U.S.'s presence in Saudi Arabia -- which is home to two of Islam's holiest shrines -- are believed to be behind two bomb attacks that have killed 24 Americans in the kingdom since June 1995.
